::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 19th 1894  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA: collection 100: box 95
:::

My dear Lady Mary
I am afraid I never heard of the name of Filian, unless it comes from the Scottish Saint Filam, St Fillan’s cave, Glenfillan. But that was a man, a Fifeshire abbot to whose good will the Scots attributed their victory at Bannockburn. At least so says [Alban Butler](other_books/otherbook_27.qmd) and [Baring Gould](other_books/otherbook_692.qmd), and the latter gives as date 7th century, I cannot get nearer. Somehow I believe there was no capital F in old time and you know some Foulkeses spelt their name ffoulkes. Our F is only the first letter with the second being up inside.[^1] If there is a Scottish connection it might account for the Filian, but I once read that about the time of Henry III people took to indulging in fanciful invented names for their daughters, so it may have come from thence.

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

A Gaelic scholar might tell you the meaning

---

[^1]: There is a sketch in illustration.
